h1: How Much Do Online Educators Earn in India? (+ Income Calculator)
dek: There is no honest average, but there is an honest formula. Work out your own online coaching income: students × price, minus the platform fee, your plan and your ads, then GST and income tax. With a free calculator and three illustrative educators.
cover_alt: How much can you earn teaching online in India: an online coaching income calculator showing gross sales, platform fee, plan cost, ads and take-home
audience: Indian educators, tutors, exam mentors, skill teachers and coaching institute owners estimating their online teaching income
author_note: Every rupee figure in this guide is illustrative and labelled so; tax rules are linked to official sources, and AllCoaching plan prices are from our own pricing page.
intro: How much you can earn teaching online in India depends on four numbers you can work out today: how many students pay you in a year, what each pays, what share your platform takes, and what you spend on your plan, ads and tools. Income = students × price × (1 − platform fee) − plan cost − ads and tools. GST and income tax come after that, depending on your turnover and income.

Nobody publishes a reliable average for Indian online educators, and any single figure would describe almost no one. An SSC maths teacher in Hindi with a YouTube channel, a spoken English coach on Instagram and a three-teacher coaching institute in Lucknow can all be teaching online and earning wildly different amounts. What they share is the arithmetic.

This guide gives you that arithmetic. You will get the formula, a calculator you can use on this page, three worked examples (all illustrative), the effect of platform fees versus plan cost, the five levers that move the number, and where GST and income tax fit in. If you are still choosing what to sell, start with what an online academy is, then come back with your own numbers.
takeaways: Online teaching income is a formula, not a salary: students × price × (1 − platform fee) − plan cost − ads and tools, before GST and income tax.
There is no honest national average for online tutor earnings in India; this guide uses illustrative numbers you can replace with your own.
Platform fee vs subscription: a percentage fee grows with your sales, a plan price does not, so the lowest-cost plan changes as you grow.

Students are usually the hardest number to move, so a free demo lesson, a test series and a next-level course often add more than a price cut.
GST registration is generally required above ₹20 lakh of turnover for services (₹10 lakh in special-category states), and income tax applies to your net income; check the official portals or a CA.

sections.h2: How do you calculate online course revenue and take-home?
sections.html:
Multiply paying students by the price to get gross sales, take off the platform fee, then subtract your plan price and what you spend on ads and tools; what is left is your take-home before tax. That is the whole method. Every section below adds detail to one part of it.

{{fig:income-formula|Online coaching income formula for India: students times price minus platform fee, plan price, ads and tools, then GST and income tax, equals take-home|Five parts, one number to plan your year on. Method only, not a promise of income.}} {{steps}}

Why gross sales is the wrong number to celebrate

Gross sales is what students paid. Take-home is what you keep. The gap between them is the platform fee, the plan, your ad spend and your tools, and later GST and income tax. An educator who plans the year on gross sales usually feels poorer than expected by Diwali, because the costs were real all along and simply were not counted.

Educators we work with often find the gap is smaller than they feared when the plan matches their sales, and larger than they expected when they paid for ads without tracking what came back. Both are fixable once the numbers are written down.

Enter how many students you expect in a year, your price, your yearly ads and tools budget, and a plan; the calculator shows gross sales, the platform fee, the plan price, your take-home before tax and which AllCoaching plan, yearly or monthly, costs least at that sales level. sections.h2: How much do online tutors earn in India? Three illustrative examples
sections.html:
These three educators are illustrative, not real people or averages: an SSC maths educator teaching in Hindi on YouTube, a spoken English coach growing on Instagram, and a small coaching institute moving its batches online. Each uses the plan that costs least at its sales level.

{{fig:three-educators|Online tutor earnings in India, three illustrative examples: SSC maths educator in Hindi on Starter, spoken English educator on Starter, coaching institute on Growth at 0% commission, with take-home before tax|Illustrative, yearly, before GST and income tax.}}

1. Exam educator teaching SSC maths in Hindi on YouTube

She posts free problem-solving videos on YouTube and sells a full SSC CGL arithmetic course for ₹1,499 on her own academy. Illustratively, 280 students buy in a year: ₹4,19,720 of sales. At that level Starter costs least. The 10% fee is ₹41,972 and the plan is ₹6,999. She spends ₹36,000 a year on a mic, editing software, a thumbnail tool and some promotion. Take-home before tax: ₹3,34,749.

Her free videos stay public on her channel, while course lessons can sit on YouTube as unlisted videos, which YouTube says "can be seen and shared by anyone with the link"1 but do not show in search. If her sales pass about ₹7.3 lakh next year, Growth at 0% commission (₹79,990 paid yearly) becomes the lower-cost plan, and she keeps 100% of every sale.

2. Skill educator teaching spoken English on Instagram

He posts short speaking tips as reels and sells a six-week interview English course at ₹1,999. Illustratively, 100 working adults buy in a year: ₹1,99,900 of sales, so yearly Starter costs least. The 10% fee is ₹19,990 and the plan is ₹6,999. He runs Meta ads at about ₹2,000 a month, ₹24,000 a year; Meta lets advertisers set a daily or lifetime budget, so this spend can be capped.4 Take-home before tax: ₹1,48,911.

3. Small coaching institute moving its batches online

A three-teacher institute runs live foundation batches at ₹8,000 a student. Illustratively, 300 students join across batches in a year: ₹24,00,000 of sales. At this level Growth costs least: 0% commission at ₹79,990 paid yearly (₹7,999 a month), with no sales limit. On Starter the same year would cost ₹2,46,999 (₹2,40,000 in fees plus the plan). With ₹1,50,000 on ads and tools, take-home before tax is ₹21,70,010, before the institute pays its teachers. If it also wants its own iOS app, Pro at ₹1,49,990 paid yearly leaves ₹21,00,010.

At this turnover, GST registration generally applies (the threshold is ₹20 lakh for most service providers), so the institute must decide whether ₹8,000 includes GST or is charged plus GST. That single choice changes take-home noticeably; our guide on GST and income tax for online tutors walks through it.

"No average will tell you what you can earn. Your own students, your own price and the plan that fits your sales will."

Amit Ratan, Founder & CEO, AllCoaching

sections.h2: Earning from online courses: which formats earn what?
sections.html:
Recorded courses and test series scale with how many students you reach; live batches and one-to-one sessions earn more per student but are limited by your hours. Most steady online incomes mix at least two.

{{fig:formats-scale|Earning from online courses in India: free demo, test series, recorded course, live batch and one-to-one, with illustrative price ranges and what each format scales with|Illustrative price ranges, not market data.}}

A recorded course is built once and sold many times, so its income depends on reach. A live batch commands a higher price because students get you in real time, but you can only run so many batches a week. One-to-one pays the most per hour and the least per week. A test series is cheap to buy and easy to add, which makes it a common second purchase for exam students.

The practical move for most educators is a ladder: a free demo lesson to earn trust, a recorded course as the main product, a test series as an add-on, and a live batch for students who want more. If you have not built the first course yet, our guide to creating your first online course covers it step by step.

sections.h2: How can you increase your online teaching income?
sections.html:
Five levers move online teaching income: price, conversion, repeat courses, test series and live batches. Change one at a time and compare take-home, not sales, after each batch.

{{fig:revenue-levers|Five levers to increase online teaching income in India: price, conversion, repeat courses, test series and live batches|Move one lever at a time.}}

1. Price

Price for the outcome a student is buying, such as clearing a cut-off or speaking confidently in an interview, not for your hours. In the SSC example, ₹1,699 instead of ₹1,499 at the same 280 students adds ₹56,000 of sales. Raise prices for the next batch, never for students who already paid.

2. Conversion

Conversion is the share of interested students who buy. A free demo lesson, a clear course page and easy checkout lift it. Students in India mostly pay by UPI, which NPCI reports processes billions of transactions every month,2 so a checkout that opens a UPI app in one tap removes a real drop-off point.

3. Repeat courses

Your next student is often your last one. A level 2 course, the next exam stage or an advanced batch sells to people who already trust you, with no ad spend.

4. Test series

A test series is a low-price add-on many exam students buy alongside a course. Illustratively, if 100 of the 280 SSC students add a ₹499 test series, that is ₹49,900 more in sales. Our guide to creating mock tests online shows how to build one.

5. Live batches

A live batch with weekly doubt classes is the premium rung. Live classes are unlimited on every AllCoaching plan, so adding one changes your hours, not your plan cost. For more on getting the students themselves, read how to sell courses online in India.

{{cta}}

Five costs come between your sales and your income: the platform fee, the plan price, payment gateway charges where they apply, ads and tools, and taxes. Most surprises come from the ones nobody wrote down.

  • Platform fee: 10% on AllCoaching Starter, 0% on Growth and Pro.
  • Plan price: paid once a year or every month, plus 18% GST on the plan.
  • Payment gateway charges: gateways such as Razorpay publish their charges on their pricing pages;3 check whether and how they apply to your plan before you price.
  • Ads and tools: Meta or Google ads, a mic, editing and design apps, a thumbnail tool.
  • Taxes: GST if you are registered, and income tax on your net income.
{{fig:income-mistakes|Common mistakes Indian educators make when calculating online teaching income, such as treating sales as income and forgetting fees, and what to do instead|Five habits that make income look bigger than it is.}}

The simplest protection is a one-page sheet: monthly sales, fees, plan, ads and tools, and what you set aside for tax. Update it on the first of every month and recheck which plan costs least once a year, at renewal.

sections.h2: What about GST and income tax on online coaching income?
sections.html:
GST and income tax are separate questions: GST depends on your yearly turnover, and income tax depends on your net income after business expenses. You can be below the GST threshold and still owe income tax.

As of 2026, GST registration is generally required once aggregate turnover from services crosses ₹20 lakh a year (₹10 lakh in special-category states), and private coaching above that is commonly taxed at 18%. The GST portal is the official place to check registration and rates.5 Income tax applies to your net taxable income under the slab you fall in, and returns are filed on the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal.6

This guide does not give tax advice. Rules, thresholds and schemes change, and your situation may differ, so read the official portals and speak to a chartered accountant before you file. Our longer explainer on GST and income tax for online tutors in India covers the basics in plain language.

faq: How much can you earn teaching online in India?

There is no reliable average. Your income is students × price × (1 − platform fee), minus your plan, ads and tools, before GST and income tax. For example, an illustrative 280 students at ₹1,499 on a 10% plan with ₹36,000 of ads and tools leaves about ₹3.35 lakh a year before tax.
How do I calculate revenue from an online course?

Multiply paying students by the price to get gross sales. Subtract the platform fee, the yearly plan price and your ads and tools to get take-home before tax. Then check GST registration and set aside income tax on your net income.
Is a platform fee better than a subscription for online courses?

It depends on your sales. A percentage fee costs little when sales are small and more as they grow, while a fixed plan price costs the same either way. On AllCoaching, Starter (₹6,999 a year + 10%) costs least below about ₹7.3 lakh of yearly sales; above that, Growth at 0% commission usually leaves you more.
Which AllCoaching plan should I choose for my income level?

Pick the plan with the lowest plan price plus platform fee at the sales you expect: Starter (₹6,999 a year + 10%) below about ₹7.3 lakh, and Growth at 0% commission (₹79,990 paid yearly, or ₹7,999 a month) above that. Choose Pro (₹14,999 a month or ₹1,49,990 paid yearly, also 0%) if you need the iOS app, 4K video or more storage. Prices exclude GST.
Do online tutors need to pay GST in India?

GST registration is generally required once aggregate turnover from services crosses ₹20 lakh a year, or ₹10 lakh in special-category states. Below that, most small tutors do not charge GST. Check the GST portal or a chartered accountant for your case.
Do I pay income tax on online teaching income?

Yes, if your net taxable income is above the basic exemption limit. Income tax applies to your income after business expenses, separately from GST, and returns are filed on the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal.
What is the fastest way to increase online coaching income?

Usually more students rather than a lower price: a free demo lesson, a clear course page and easy UPI checkout raise conversion. Then add a test series or a next-level course for students who already trust you.
Can I try AllCoaching before choosing a plan?

Yes. Every plan starts with a 7-day free trial and no card is needed to start. You can build your academy and add a course, then choose Starter with a 10% platform fee, or Growth or Pro at 0% commission, paid monthly or yearly.
